text: When raising a nursery specifically for seed multiplication, site selection matters as much as bed construction. Choose a plot with full sun (not shaded), fertile soil, close to a reliable water source, and free of volunteer seedlings from other rice varieties. If a farmer is raising more than one variety's nursery in adjacent plots, either keep them physically far apart or separated by a clear path/bund, or stagger the sowing dates so the two lots are visually distinguishable and easy to tell apart when weeding or pulling seedlings. Three bed types are used: Wet bed (ថ្នាលទឹក) - plough and puddle the soil to a fine, even tilth, then sun-dry the field 7-10 days and clear weeds before final leveling; work in about 200 kg of well-decomposed organic/compost manure per 100 m² (roughly 1 are), spread evenly, and cut shallow furrows through the bed to help drain and re-flood it easily. Dry bed (ថ្នាលគោក) - same land preparation as the wet bed (plough, sun-dry 7-10 days, clear weeds, level), with the same rate of organic manure worked in; the bed itself is raised, 1.2-1.5 m wide and 4-5 cm high, with length depending on the plot's size and shape. Mudball/tray-style bed (ថ្នាល ដាក់ប៉ុក) - mix soil (50%), well-decomposed compost (30%), and rice husk ash that has been soaked in water for 24 hours to remove harmful salts (20%), and blend thoroughly; edge the bed with bamboo strips or boards about 3 cm high to keep the soil mix from washing off; line the base with banana leaf or plastic sheeting so seedling roots cannot penetrate the ground beneath, which makes pulling seedlings later much easier and gentler on the roots; make the bed about 1 m wide and 5-10 m long depending on space, spread the soil mix about 3 cm thick on top, then compact it evenly. For a 1-hectare transplanting area, plan roughly 30-40 kg of seed sown across 150-200 m² of nursery bed. These figures are illustrative starting points; farmers should check current CARDI or extension guidance for field-specific decisions.
